title: Design System: Star Cinema 星辉影城

display.purpose: The single largest headline — admin welcome. Nothing competes at this size.

title.purpose: Section headings, always with the 3px ink bar on the left edge.

headline.purpose: The two-character brand mark, widened by 2px tracking.

body.purpose: Default voice: paragraphs, labels, table cells, buttons.

label.purpose: Ticket numbers, showtimes, amounts, countdowns, seat and grid coordinates.

shadows.name: paper-lift
shadows.purpose: Rest state of every card and ticket — reads as the sheet's own thickness.

shadows.name: paper-lift-hover
shadows.purpose: Hover only, and only on cards that are genuinely interactive.

shadows.name: modal
shadows.purpose: Dialogs, message boxes, poppers, toasts — the only convincing shadow in the system.

shadows.name: hall-edge
shadows.purpose: Single-pixel separation inside the dark auditorium panel.

motion.name: transition-fast
motion.purpose: Colour transitions on buttons, links, chips, seats — the default.

motion.name: conflict-flash
motion.purpose: How long a seat taken by someone else keeps its red pulsing ring.

motion.name: reduced-motion
motion.purpose: Global override for prefers-reduced-motion; do not remove.

components.name: Primary Button
components.description: The single ink action. Darkens on hover; never lifts, glows, or gradients.

narrative.overview:
This is a piece of printed matter that happens to be on a screen. Every surface behaves like a cinema ticket that has been through a press: cold grey-white paper stock, exactly one ink colour, hairline rules doing all the structural work, and a perforated tear separating the stub from the ticket body. Nothing floats. Nothing glows. A card is a sheet lying on other sheets, and the only thing that distinguishes it is that it is a shade brighter than what's underneath.

The density is that of a box-office counter — information-dense, aligned, unemotional, and quick to scan. Structure comes from 1px rules and tonal steps rather than shadows, gradients, or fills; the tabular rhythm is carried by monospaced figures so that ticket numbers, showtimes, amounts and countdowns never reflow when a digit changes. Expression is spent in exactly two places: the single royal-blue ink, and the small library of physical printing devices (perforation notches, mono ticket numbers, the short ink bar that opens a section).

The one deliberate exception is the auditorium: the seat map is a single dark ticket face mounted on the paper, and the admin sidebar is its structural twin. That dark family is the same ink colour inverted, not a second identity — it exists so five saturated seat states stay separable instead of collapsing into grey.
keyCharacteristics: Cold grey-white paper stock. Never warm, never cream.
Exactly one ink colour. Its rarity is the point.
Hairline 1px rules carry structure; shadows do not.
Monospaced tabular figures for anything that must not reflow.
One dark family (#0f172a) shared by the admin sidebar and the auditorium panel.
Perforated tear notches as the recurring signature device.
Near-zero corner radii — a printed sheet has no rounded corners.

rules.name: The One Ink Rule
rules.body: There is one accent. It is applied to less than a tenth of any given screen, and it is never duplicated by a second hue. When something needs emphasis and blue is already spent, reach for a heavier rule weight or a darker ink, not a new colour.

rules.name: The Inverted Family Rule
rules.body: Dark surfaces are the ink colour inverted, never a new palette. The sidebar and the auditorium must stay the same value, because it is one family.

rules.name: The Slash-Syntax Rule
rules.body: Alpha is composed as rgb(var(--x-rgb) / a). The comma form rgba(var(--x-rgb), a) is invalid CSS — the browser drops the declaration silently and the surface turns transparent.

rules.name: The Ticket Number Rule
rules.body: Anything that is a number on this system is set in mono with font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums — order numbers, showtimes, amounts, countdowns, seat labels, row/column labels, and dashboard statistics. Proportional figures are a bug here: a ticking countdown must not move its own frame.

rules.name: The Two-Voice Rule
rules.body: Serif is for headings and the brand mark only. Body copy never sets in serif, and headings never set in the body sans. The contrast between the two is the hierarchy.

rules.name: The Flat-By-Default Rule
rules.body: Surfaces are flat at rest. Nothing lifts, glows, or translates on hover — a primary button answers with a darker ink, not a raised one. The only motion permitted on a surface is a colour transition.

dos: Do route every colour through the :root tokens in src/styles/main.css. Changing a token changes the whole site, including the Element Plus ramp, the chart series, and the favicon.
Do compose alpha as rgb(var(--x-rgb) / a).
Do keep the single ink at under a tenth of any screen, and answer "I need more emphasis" with a heavier rule or a darker ink.
Do set every figure that can change in mono with tabular figures.
Do give seat states and any colour-coded status a non-colour channel (edge weight, dash, stripe, bar) alongside the fill.
Do keep the five seat grounds at adjacent grayscale gaps ≥2/255.
Do reuse the shared seat/legend token pair rather than restating seat colours in the legend.
Do draw a visible focus ring on any dark surface; Element Plus's default disappears there.
Do honour prefers-reduced-motion — it is already wired globally.
donts: Don't hard-code a colour in a .vue file. The only permitted literals are the payment QR code's white and #111827 and the token declarations themselves.
Don't add a second brand colour. Exactly six --accent* declarations exist in :root; a seventh fails the test suite.
Don't lift, translate, glow, or gradient a primary action on hover. Darken the ink instead.
Don't use colourful emoji as icons, decoration, or section markers.
Don't put a solid blue block on the dark sidebar as an active state; use the tint plus the 3px inset bar.
Don't reintroduce a shadow as rest-state decoration on a non-overlay surface.
Don't round a corner past 6px, or give a sheet a pill silhouette.
Don't set body copy in the display serif, or a heading in the body sans.
Don't change any --seat-* value without re-running the grayscale-separation assertion.
Don't delete the table's white-space: nowrap rule — it is a functional fix that stops snowflake IDs from wrapping and inflating table rows, not a style preference.
